meta.description: Lead-time test: does the growth of US imports from an economy improve a same-month estimate of that economy's own total export growth over a persistence baseline, on months after the fitting period?

sources.name: US Census Bureau, International Trade (monthly imports by Harmonized System)
sources.licence: Census Bureau Data API Terms of Service (https://www.census.gov/data/developers/terms-of-service.html). Products must show the notice "This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau", must not misrepresent the data while naming the Bureau as its source, and must not use the data to identify a person or business. The trade pages carry the notice. The terms set no numeric request limit; this pipeline makes sixteen calls at most once every six days.
sources.frequency: fetched at most once every six days; Census publishes once a month
sources.typical_lag: about five weeks after the month ends

sources.name: IMF data (International Trade in Goods, International Liquidity, Consumer Price Index)
sources.licence: IMF Copyright and Usage, Special Terms for Statistical Data (https://www.imf.org/en/about/copyright-and-terms). Users may download, copy, create derivative works, publish and distribute IMF data, with attribution in the form "Source: International Monetary Fund, <dataset>, <link>", saying so when the data are materially transformed, and without altering the data in a way that affects their accuracy. Commercial reuse needs the IMF's permission (copyright@imf.org). The general site terms also forbid bulk download by automated means without permission; this pipeline asks the public SDMX API for 19 series a day, which is not a bulk download of the database, but the IMF has not been asked to confirm that. The site is non-commercial and cites the IMF under every table.
sources.typical_lag: one to five months (trade is slowest)

limitations: Scored on today's revised figures for both series, not on the values first published, so the test is kinder than real time.
The economy's own exports are its exports to every country; the US is only one buyer, so a weak link is expected for economies that sell little to it.
The baseline assumes the economy's own figure is exactly one month behind. When it is further behind, US imports are worth more than this test shows.

finding.label: observation
finding.reason: No signal found: for no economy did US imports beat the persistence baseline by more than twice the standard error of the gain. The correlations are shown as observations.
